text: Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisementHistoryArchaeologists Unravel an 88-Year-Old Murder MysteryThe killing of James Leslie StarkeyJCBy Jake Currie5:00 PM CST on November 4, 2026Add Nautilus to GoogleAround midday on January 10, 1938, renowned British archaeologist James Leslie Starkey called for a taxi to take him to the city of Jerusalem from Lasich, the ancient Canaanite and Israelite settlement he had been studying. Outside of Hebron, Starkey’s driver spotted five armed men with white headscarves covering their faces. They shot at the cab, and with the road too narrow to turn around, Starkey and the driver were trapped. The men beckoned the car to approach and then ordered both of them to exit. Once Starkey and the driver identified themselves, the band of brigands let the driver go. Starkey was later found dead. Powered By 10 ShareNextStayBritish authorities investigating the murder focused on Issa al-Battat, a Palestinian rebel commander who had found himself on the wrong side of the ruling authority before. He commanded dozens of fighters, collected protection money from local villages, and had attacked a British police commander on a nearby road just a year earlier.
